speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail; being the restrained driver of the rear car suggests significant hyperextension force. You mentioned knee pain as well—can you describe the specific position the right leg feels "stuck" in, and does the foot point upward while the knee extends?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: That "shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated" position is highly suggestive of a hip dislocation, likely traumatic posterior hip dislocation with an associated femoral neck fracture. I need to confirm if you have any numbness or tingling in your foot, as this could indicate femoral nerve injury. REQUEST TEST: X_Pelvis_AAP (Anteroposterior view).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic X-ray (Anteroposterior view): No fractures identified in the pelvic ring or femoral neck. However, alignment findings suggest posterior dislocation of the right hip.
